manifest.name: Point of Sale
manifest.summary: Handle checkouts and payments for shops and restaurants.

behavioral_notes.observation: POS orders are created in the OWL browser app while offline and pushed to the server via the `sync_from_ui` RPC, which calls `_process_order` (create-or-update keyed by uuid; draft orders may be overwritten, non-draft are discarded as duplicates). On a non-draft, non-cancel order `_process_saved_order` runs `action_pos_order_paid` -> `_create_order_picking` (real-time stock.picking unless `update_stock_at_closing`) -> `_compute_total_cost_in_real_time`, and if `to_invoice` it calls `_generate_pos_order_invoice` to post an account.move. None of this offline-create-then-sync semantics is visible in metadata.

A session is the cash-control + accounting envelope around a day of selling. On open, if `config_id.cash_control`, the opening float is seeded from the previous session's `cash_register_balance_end_real`. Closing (`action_pos_session_closing_control`) blocks while draft orders exist, counts cash via `post_closing_cash_details`, then `_validate_session` creates pickings at closing (if `update_stock_at_closing`), computes costs, and calls `_create_account_move` which builds one consolidated account.move with receivable/cash/pay-later/invoice/stock-valuation lines and reconciles them; an unbalanced move rolls back and opens the close wizard. Cash in/out (`try_cash_in_out`) writes account.bank.statement.line records gated by `_has_cash_move_permission`. These multi-model side-effects are pure Python.

pos.config is a fat (~98-field) terminal profile that wires the till to a stock.picking.type, sales journal, invoice journal, pricelist, payment methods and hardware (cash drawer / scale / printer / IoT proxy). Many `module_pos_*` Boolean fields (pos_restaurant, pos_hr, pos_discount, pos_avatax, plus payment add-ons pos_adyen/pos_stripe/pos_viva_com/pos_razorpay/pos_mercado_pago etc. on res.config.settings) are install-triggers: toggling them installs the corresponding bridge module, so a single config silently extends the schema/behavior of the whole subsystem.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (offline-first OWL POS app) -- gap #3 exemplar
behavioral_notes.observation: The entire POS UI is a standalone OWL single-page app served at /pos/ui (entry: static/src/app/main.js + pos_app.js, root component Chrome) with its own client-side ORM (static/src/app/models/related_models/) persisting to IndexedDB (models/utils/indexed_db.js) and a service-worker, so the cashier keeps ringing sales with no network. 166 JS files / 78 XML templates / ~43 components in the point_of_sale._assets_pos bundle, ~30 registry services/screens, dedicated offline/rpc error handlers, plus a second customer_display app. Almost none of this client logic (screen flow, buffered orders, offline queue, hardware proxy) is reverse-engineerable from Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: point_of_sale (Point of Sale application component: backend ORM + offline OWL POS terminal app)
information_flows: depends: stock_account, resource, barcodes, digest, iot_base, partner_autocomplete, phone_validation, html_editor, google_address_autocomplete
side-effect: pos.order.sync_from_ui -> create/update pos.order -> stock.picking (delivery) [+ account.move if to_invoice]
side-effect: pos.session close (_validate_session -> _create_account_move) -> consolidated account.move + reconciled receivable/cash/stock-valuation lines [+ pickings at closing]
offline path: OWL app persists orders to IndexedDB and replays them to /pos via sync_from_ui when reconnected

capabilities: Operate Point-of-Sale Checkout (ring up & tender sales)
Manage Till Sessions & Cash Control (open/close, count, cash in/out)
Accept Multi-method Payments (cash, card terminal, QR, pay-later)
Fulfil & Decrement Stock from the sale
value_streams: Sell-at-Counter: open session -> scan/select products -> tender payment -> print receipt / invoice -> deliver goods (stock move) -> close session (cash count + journal entry)
policies: 12 record rules: multi-company + session/own-document scoping on pos.order, pos.session, pos.payment
cash in/out and cash-move delete gated by _has_cash_move_permission / _has_cash_delete_permission
cannot close a session while draft orders remain; maximum cash difference can be enforced (set_maximum_difference / amount_authorized_diff)
metrics: report.pos.order (Point of Sale Orders analysis: amounts, qty, margin, discount)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: Point of Sale is a value-chain primary activity: its core act is the retail sell/checkout transaction that converts demand into a paid pos.order, then drives the downstream chain operations -- outbound delivery (stock.picking) and revenue/cash recognition (account.move at session close). Mapped to APQC 3.0 (Market and Sell) because the dominant, originating operation is the in-store sale at the counter (the 3.5 'manage sales orders' family realized as a till), mirroring the `sale` module; the deliver (APQC 4.0 / stock) and accounts-receivable + cash (APQC 9.0 / account) steps are real but are triggered side-effects of the sale, not POS's primary mission. Note the heavy network/frontend character: POS is delivered as an offline-first OWL single-page app with a client-side ORM, IndexedDB queue and hardware/IoT proxy, giving it strong 'shop' (service-encounter) and 'network' (terminal mediating buyer/payment infrastructure) overtones even though the value logic is chain.

standard_capabilities: session lifecycle with opening float, cash counting and closing control
multi payment methods incl. external card terminals (Adyen/Stripe/Viva/Razorpay/Mercado Pago) and QR
automatic stock delivery (real-time or at session closing) via stock_account
receipt printing (browser / ePOS / IoT proxy) and customer-facing display
refunds, tips, pricelists, fiscal positions, combos and product attributes
consolidated accounting closing entry per session + optional per-order invoicing
POS sales reporting (orders report, daily Z-report, digest KPI)
typical_fits: retail / restaurant counter checkout with cash + card
single sale -> delivery -> invoice/cash flow per till
multi-till / multi-company scoping via record rules and pos.config
feature add-ons toggled via module_pos_* flags (restaurant, hr, discount, avatax)
common_gaps: bespoke loyalty / promotion logic beyond standard pricelists and pos_discount
integration with a non-supported payment terminal or fiscal printer (custom IoT/driver)
country-specific fiscal/tax certification (signed receipts, fiscal data module)
custom offline-sync conflict resolution or extra client-side screens (OWL dev, not config)
non-standard hardware (scales, scanners) outside the hardware_proxy/IoT model
drive_hints: curl jsonrpc /pos/ping (auth=user) to confirm a live terminal heartbeat
browse /pos/ui/<config_id> to launch the OWL terminal app

open_questions: Exact pos.order state machine (draft/paid/done/invoiced/cancel) and which transitions the OWL app drives vs. the server.
How update_stock_at_closing vs real-time picking is decided per company/config and its inventory-valuation impact.
Full set of account.move lines and reconciliations produced by _create_account_move at session close (per payment method / stock valuation).
Behavior of the offline IndexedDB queue under conflict (two devices, same uuid) and the rescue-session recovery path.
Which module_pos_* add-ons are present in this deployment and how they extend the base schema/UI.
